thread:
jamie_oncall: APAC (ap-southeast1) - seeing sustained GPU node evictions in pool-gpu-1 across rack=5 and rack=6. Autoscaler is draining and new pods fail to provision. Impact: ~25% increase in latency and intermittent 503s. Triage in progress, opening bridge now.

deploy-bot: Incident created: #INC-2045 ap-southeast1 GPU provisioning failures — bridge: <https://meet.redwood.ai/bridge/INC-2045>

maria_infra: Observed upstream ToR switch flaps; BGP sessions are resetting to the affected racks. Some hosts lost mgmt connectivity, syslogs show kernel oops on one box. Evictions line up with network interruptions. Pulling dmesg/syslog now.

jamie_oncall: Can we isolate to rack=5/6? If fabric is flappy I'd prefer cordon+evacuate those racks and redirect new allocations to ap-east1 and us-west2. Any objections?

lee_support: Support queue: top APAC customers reporting increased 502/503. Tickets spiking. Recommend status page update + targeted email to impacted customers. We need a short ETA for comms.

kai_commops: Drafting status page copy. Proposed public ETA 3-4 hours for full recovery (vendor + rack rebuild). Would prefer a conservative estimate. Sending draft in thread.

anuja_product: Note: Dedicated customers pinned to reserved pools may be unaffected. For hosted customers, we could consider routing to a quantized model variant (q4_0) for non-SLA tiers to reduce GPU mem pressure and speed scheduling. Quality tradeoff — opt-in or infra-level tiered fallback?

maria_infra: We can flip routing for non-SLA tiers at the infra layer. Will need a quick config change in routing rules. Recommend enabling only for burst/low-tier to avoid broad regressions. I'll prepare a rollout script.

ops_lead: Agreed on cross-region shift + tiered quality fallback. Priorities: 1) stabilize latency 2) minimize customer disruption 3) limit cross-region egress cost. Kai, pls include a short cost-implication note in comms so Enterprise teams aren't surprised.

jamie_oncall: Action list:
- cordon+evacuate rack=5/6 nodes (maria)
- set autoscaler to 'no-provision' in ap-southeast1 (jamie)
- enable cross-region routing to ap-east1/us-west2 for new allocations (maria)
- enable q4 fallback for non-SLA tiers (maria/anuja)
- update status page + targeted email (kai)
- open support bridge & post template (lee)
Bridge: <https://meet.redwood.ai/bridge/INC-2045>

maria_infra: Cordon/drain started. Command used: `for n in $(kubectl get nodes -l rack=5 -o name); do kubectl cordon $n && kubectl drain $n --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data; done` — drains are rolling. Found one node with `kernel: oom_reaper` followed by `nvidia: GPU reset` in syslog. Vendor ticket opened.

autoscale-bot: Autoscaler paused for ap-southeast1. Policy set: `no-provision` for 2h. New pods scheduled to ap-east1/us-west2 where capacity is available.

lee_support: Support template (please review):
---
Hello <Customer>,
We’re investigating an infrastructure issue affecting GPU provisioning in our APAC region (ap-southeast1). Some requests may experience increased latency or transient errors. We’ve redirected traffic to nearby regions and expect progressive recovery in ~3–4 hours. We will send updates every 30 minutes. Apologies for the disruption — if this is causing critical impact please reply and we will prioritize a workaround.
---
Approve to send to impacted customers?

kai_commops: Status page draft (posted as update 1):
```
Incident #INC-2045 — APAC GPU provisioning failures
Status: Partial outage impacting inference latency and availability in ap-southeast1.
What we know: An upstream rack switch experienced repeated BGP session resets causing node mgmt disconnects and subsequent GPU node evictions in several racks. We are evacuating affected racks and shifting traffic to ap-east1 and us-west2.
Impact: Increased latency and intermittent 5xx for some customers in APAC.
Mitigation: Nodes cordoned and drained, autoscaler paused, cross-region routing enabled. Tiered fallback to quantized models enabled for non-SLA customers to reduce scheduling pressure.
ETA: ~3–4 hours for full recovery. Next update in 30 minutes.
```

jamie_oncall: Approve both support template and status page. Also include a note: "We may see increased cross-region egress charges while routing traffic. We’re evaluating credits for impacted accounts." Next update in 30m.

ops_lead: Finance ok to approve small goodwill credits for impacted Enterprise customers. Work with finance on manual adjustments after incident.

maria_infra: Vendor ETA: approx 2h onsite for TOR replacement and burn-in. With replacement + health checks we expect racks stable in ~3.5h. Will only reintroduce nodes after passing `node-e2e-healthcheck` and 10m of green metrics.

jamie_oncall: Updating status page now. Next update at +30m or on milestone. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

kai_commops: Status page updated: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2045 — posted update + emailed affected list.

lee_support: Support notified top impacted customers and created prioritized queue. Early responses: a handful asked to route to EU instead; others accepted fallback to quantized model. Continuing to triage.

maria_infra: Early metrics: after shift queue length down ~15% and error rate trending down, tail latency still elevated (~2.1s p95). We'll keep monitoring while vendor works on rack. Sample error observed: `X-Error: connection reset by peer` from pod kubelet logs.

jamie_oncall: Keeping bridge open for now; follow-ups: postmortem runbook (ops_lead), update SLA communications (anuja). Thanks all for quick response. :thumbsup:
